name: Vegetable frittata
summary: An oven-finished Italian omelette packed with red pepper, baby marrow, spinach and cherry tomatoes under a little feta, served warm in wedges or cold the next day.
about: A frittata is the Italian open omelette, started on the stove and finished in the oven so it sets right through. It is a good way to use up the vegetables at the end of the week, and a cold wedge travels well in a lunchbox.

ingredients.name: Baby marrows
ingredients.note: about 200 g, halved lengthways and sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Heat the olive oil in a 24–26 cm ovenproof non-stick frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the red pepper and baby marrows and cook, stirring now and then, for 5 minutes, until tender and any liquid has cooked off. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and spinach and stir for 1–2 minutes, until the spinach has wilted. Spread the vegetables evenly over the base of the pan.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a jug until no streaks of white remain. Turn the heat to medium-low, pour the eggs over the vegetables and scatter the feta on top.
Cook without stirring for 4 minutes, until the edge is set and pale gold underneath when you lift it with a spatula.

Move the pan to the oven and bake for 12–15 minutes, until puffed and set in the centre with no wobble; a knife pushed into the middle should come out clean. The handle will be hot, so use an oven glove.
Leave to rest for 5 minutes, then loosen the edge and slide the frittata onto a board. Toss the salad leaves and cucumber with the olive oil and lemon juice and serve with wedges of frittata.
prepNote: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; eat it cold in a lunchbox or warm a wedge through in the microwave.
